articles.title: Agent4Crypto: How Dual-Reflective Trading Agents Handle Non-Stationary Market Regimes Without Retraining
articles.excerpt: Cryptocurrency markets run 24/7 at machine speed with no circuit breakers. Market regimes flip from bull to bear faster than you can retrain a model. Agent4Crypto addresses this by splitting reflectio…
articles.body: Cryptocurrency markets run 24/7 at machine speed with no circuit breakers. Market regimes flip from bull to bear faster than you can retrain a model. Agent4Crypto addresses this by splitting reflection into two loops: one that critiques past decisions and stores lessons, another that measures which agent style (aggressive, neutral, conservative) is currently aligned with market behavior. A PPO-based gating policy dynamically weights the three trader agents without hardcoded voting rules. The architecture matters because most LLM trading agents either use single-pass decisions (no feedback) or fixed aggregation rules that break when volatility spikes.

articles.title: DBDelve's Rust and GPUI Stack: What Building a Database Client Reveals About Agent Tool Interface Design
articles.excerpt: DBDelve is a Rust-based database client built on GPUI, the UI framework from the Zed editor team. It launched on Show HN with 107 points and 40 comments, positioning itself as a performance-focused al…
articles.body: DBDelve is a Rust-based database client built on GPUI, the UI framework from the Zed editor team. It launched on Show HN with 107 points and 40 comments, positioning itself as a performance-focused alternative to DBeaver and Electron-based tools. The architecture choices matter beyond speed benchmarks. They expose design patterns for building developer tools that need to serve both human workflows and programmatic agent access. The project claims a 1.1-second launch versus DBeaver's 5.2 seconds, 133 MB idle memory versus 606 MB, and 0.21-second query execution for 1,000 rows versus 1.96 seconds. For a 1-million-row table with 100 columns, DBDelve uses 4.9 GB versus DBeaver's 17 GB.

articles.excerpt: Most "accept crypto" guides start with a payment processor. That's fine, but for Monero there's a simpler option that a lot of developers miss: the official monero-wallet-rpc can do almost everything…
articles.body: Most "accept crypto" guides start with a payment processor. That's fine, but for Monero there's a simpler option that a lot of developers miss: the official monero-wallet-rpc can do almost everything a small shop needs. You don't need a third party, an account, or extra fees, and nobody else sees your orders. The idea is simple: every order gets its own subaddress. When a payment lands on that subaddress, you know exactly which order it belongs to. You don't need payment IDs, unique amounts, or to ask customers to type a memo. This post walks through the whole flow with working Python. Why one subaddress per order works A Monero wallet can generate practically unlimited subaddresses (they start with 8).

articles.body: Un circuit concret pour les cabinets et commerces marocains qui travaillent sur rendez-vous : dentistes, kinés, opticiens, garages, instituts de beauté. Dans beaucoup de cabinets au Maroc, l'agenda est tenu sur un logiciel, un Google Agenda ou même un cahier, et les rappels se font à la main, la veille, par téléphone ou WhatsApp. Quand la secrétaire est débordée, les rappels sautent. C'est d'automatiser la partie répétitive (confirmer, rappeler, enregistrer la réponse) et de laisser à l'humain ce qui demande du jugement : déplacer un rendez-vous compliqué, répondre à une question médicale, gérer un patient mécontent.

articles.title: Snowflake's AI Agents Fix Pipelines: Data Engineer Impact
articles.excerpt: The first time I trusted an automated "fix" to a pipeline, it fixed the error, and the fix was wrong. The job went green. The row counts didn't. It took 3 weeks and an angry finance analyst before any…
articles.body: The first time I trusted an automated "fix" to a pipeline, it fixed the error, and the fix was wrong. The job went green. The row counts didn't. It took 3 weeks and an angry finance analyst before anyone noticed that the dedupe logic had been "simplified" right out of existence. So when Snowflake announced on Nov 3 that AI agents would now investigate failed pipelines and rewrite Spark jobs for you, I didn't panic. I did what I always do: I read the release notes, the docs, and the footnotes. My take is that this launch makes the Data Engineer who can review a change and own it worth more than before, while the engineer whose whole value is typing out the fix gets cheaper. Your next interview loop will start to reflect that.

Galadriel finds herself hiding in a hedge from a Nazgnagôl, the still-living precursors to the Ringwraiths that would put Frodo and his Hobbit friends in the exact same position.
